name: Renal Countercurrent Mechanism and ADH Regulation

reference.source: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology / Vander's Renal Physiology
clinicalPearls: Countercurrent multiplier in juxtamedullary nephrons creates an hyperosmotic medullary interstitium reaching 1200 mOsm/kg at papilla
Descending thin limb is water-permeable and solute-impermeable; thick ascending limb is water-impermeable and actively pumps NaCl
Vasa recta hairpin capillary loops act as countercurrent exchangers, preserving the medullary gradient while supplying nutrients
ADH (vasopressin) binds basolateral V2 receptors on principal cells, stimulating cAMP/PKA to insert aquaporin-2 water channels apically
Urea recycling via ADH-stimulated UT-A1/UT-A3 transporters provides 40-50% of inner medullary interstitial hyperosmolality
reference.pathophysiology: Central diabetes insipidus arises from defective synthesis or release of ADH by hypothalamic supraoptic/paraventricular nuclei. Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus involves renal insensitivity to ADH due to V2 receptor mutations or lithium therapy. SIADH involves unsuppressed ADH secretion, causing euvolemic hyponatremia with inappropriately concentrated urine.
additionalInvestigations: Water deprivation test with desmopressin challenge
Paired plasma and urine osmolality with urinary sodium concentration
Copeptin measurement as a surrogate for arginine vasopressin
